Implemented, not yet run through optimize_cfd_mean_reversion.py's TRAIN/TEST validation -- same starting point donchian_breakout@v1 had before its own grid search found v2. Params are reasonable, sourced placeholders (see mean_reversion.py's docstring), not validated numbers.

optimize_cfd_mean_reversion.py's TRAIN/TEST grid search (81 combinations across band_window/band_std/atr_stop_mult/atr_target_mult) found zero combinations with positive CAGR and drawdown within the -25% cap on ~2 years of H1 forex/gold data (yfinance proxy feed). Baseline (default params) alone: TRAIN cagr=-83.8% maxdd=-97.8% sharpe=-6.37, TEST cagr=-81.2% maxdd=-76.8% sharpe=-6.03. This specific Bollinger-Band mean-reversion formulation shows no usable edge on this data -- retiring rather than leaving it as a misleadingly-still-viable CANDIDATE nobody is going to test further. The ranging regime is back to having zero suited ACTIVE or CANDIDATE strategy; a genuine open gap, not a solved one -- see docs/ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT.md gap #11.

Implemented (via a GitHub PR built to a spec from this session, reviewed and merged), not yet run through optimize_cfd_rsi_reversion.py's TRAIN/TEST validation -- same starting point every other CFD strategy had before its own grid search. A second, structurally distinct attempt at the 'ranging' regime after mean_reversion@v1's honest negative result: fades RSI momentum exhaustion behind an ADX flat-market gate, not Bollinger-band price deviation. Params are reasonable, sourced placeholders (see rsi_reversion.py's docstring), not validated numbers.

optimize_cfd_rsi_reversion.py's TRAIN/TEST grid search (243 combinations) found only 1/108 TRAIN-qualifying candidates, and that one candidate (rsi_oversold=30, rsi_overbought=75, adx_flat_threshold=15, atr_stop_mult=1.5, atr_target_mult=2.5; TRAIN cagr=1.4% maxdd=-3.2%) failed out-of-sample: TEST cagr=-6.8% maxdd=-6.8% win_rate=14.3% (7 trades) -- OVERFIT, not robust. Baseline (default params) was mild rather than catastrophic (TRAIN cagr=-1.1%, TEST cagr=+1.9% on only 11/3 trades -- too few to mean anything). No combination held up out-of-sample -- retiring rather than leaving it as a misleadingly-still-viable CANDIDATE, same honest-negative-result treatment mean_reversion@v1 got. The ranging regime is still without a suited ACTIVE or CANDIDATE strategy; two structurally distinct approaches (Bollinger-band fade, RSI+ADX fade) have now been ruled out on this data, not just one.

Implemented (proposed by GPT in GitHub issue #5's joint design discussion, built by this session), not yet run through optimize_cfd_support_resistance.py's TRAIN/TEST validation -- same starting point every other CFD strategy had before its own grid search. Third attempt at the 'ranging' regime, and the first with a genuinely different data representation from the first two: confirmed swing-high/swing-low price structure, not a derived statistic over closes (mean_reversion@v1's Bollinger bands, rsi_reversion@v1's RSI oscillator). Params are reasonable, sourced placeholders (see support_resistance.py's docstring), not validated numbers.

Bug-fixed grid search (81 combinations, real TRAIN/TEST split, run 35512685177): 0/81 combinations cleared even the cheap TRAIN gate (min trades, CAGR>0, drawdown within -25% cap). Baseline itself TRAIN cagr=-91.8% maxdd=-99.5% win_rate=48.1% trades=2714, TEST cagr=-94.5% maxdd=-91.4% win_rate=45.4% trades=1172 -- near account wipeout on both splits. Third structurally distinct ranging-regime approach (after mean_reversion@v1 and rsi_reversion@v1, both also RETIRED) to be honestly ruled out on this data, not left as a misleadingly-still-viable CANDIDATE.
